lines.trans: Hi, Max! I thought you were avoiding me.
I have already missed you very much.
Whoa, it seems to me you are rushing a little.
I do not understand, what are you talking about?
I mean the fact that you kissed me.
Wait, is all of this because of Vika right now?
Are you afraid that she will fire both of us?
I am not worried for myself, but for you.
I do not want you to be left without a job.
Thank you so much for worrying about me.
Well great, now I am tangled up even worse.
Chef, did you show her who is boss in the kitchen?

meanings.en: to miss someone (+ по + dat.), to start missing
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оскучиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'missed (you)', paired with 'скучать'.

examples.trans: Do you think I didn't miss you? I'm already climbing the wall!

examples.text: Как ты думаешь, ради кого она вернулась?
examples.trans: Who do you think she came back for?

examples.text: Ты думаешь, она вернулась сюда ради меня?
examples.trans: Do you think she came back here for me?

examples.text: Вика, можно тебя попросить на одну секунду?
examples.trans: Vika, may I have a word with you for one second?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот твой новый электронный пропуск, держи.
examples.trans: Here is your new electronic pass, take it.

examples.text: Уже соблюдают. Вот это твой комплект.
examples.trans: They are already following them. Here is your kit.

examples.text: Вот твой коктейль, бери и иди отсюда.
examples.trans: Here is your cocktail, take it and go away.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы что, теперь на заводе работаем?
examples.trans: What, do we work at a factory now?

examples.text: Нам теперь и покурить нельзя сходить?
examples.trans: Can we not even go out for a smoke now?

examples.text: Теперь у нашего ресторана совсем другие хозяева.
examples.trans: Now our restaurant has completely different owners.

meanings.en: to get confused, to become muddled
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'путаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'got confused', paired with 'запутываться'.

examples.text: Я совсем запутался в этих правилах.
examples.trans: I got completely confused by these rules.

examples.text: Чёрт, я запутался. Это опасная идея.
examples.trans: Darn, I am confused. This is a dangerous idea.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А это ещё что такое в коридоре?
examples.trans: And what on earth is that in the corridor?

examples.text: Ты не поняла? Что тебе ещё надо?
examples.trans: You did not get it? What else do you need?

examples.text: Нет, я могу с радостью ещё продолжить.
examples.trans: No, I can gladly continue some more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (polite/plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Доброе утро, Виктор Петрович, вы сегодня опаздываете.
examples.trans: Good morning, Viktor Petrovich, you are late today.

examples.text: Вот твой новый электронный пропуск, держи.
examples.trans: Here is your new electronic pass, take it.

examples.text: Новые правила строго запрещают нам это делать.
examples.trans: The new rules strictly forbid us to do that.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.text: Шеф, вы ей показали, кто главный на кухне?
examples.trans: Chef, did you show her who is boss in the kitchen?

examples.text: Покажите руки!
examples.trans: Show me your hands!

examples.text: Покажем это Аникееву?
examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Доброе утро, Виктор Петрович, вы сегодня опаздываете.
examples.trans: Good morning, Viktor Petrovich, you are late today.

examples.text: Неужели кто-то будет соблюдать твои дурацкие правила?
examples.trans: Will anyone really follow your foolish rules?

examples.text: Виктория Сергеевна ведь сказала, что нельзя выходить.
examples.trans: Viktoriya Sergeyevna said that we cannot go outside.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main').

examples.text: Для меня это самое главное в жизни.
examples.trans: For me that is the most important thing in life.

examples.text: Шеф, вы ей показали, кто главный на кухне?
examples.trans: Chef, did you show her who is boss in the kitchen?

examples.text: Но самое главное, что вы изменили своим принципам.
examples.trans: But the main thing is that you betrayed your principles.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Перемены могут начаться абсолютно в любой момент.
examples.trans: Changes can begin at absolutely any moment.

examples.text: У нас вводятся общие правила этой сети.
examples.trans: The general rules of this chain are being introduced here.

examples.text: Мы что, теперь на заводе работаем?
examples.trans: What, do we work at a factory now?

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Что за беспредел устроили у меня на кухне?
examples.trans: What kind of chaos have they caused in my kitchen?

examples.text: Кухня, внимание! Запомните все мои слова!
examples.trans: Kitchen, attention! Everyone remember my words!

examples.text: Шеф, вы ей показали, кто главный на кухне?
examples.trans: Chef, did you show her who is boss in the kitchen?
